findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope is added to the CLIENTS resource type and wired into canMapClientScopeRoles(), but no test in this diff exercises it. The test suite covers MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE (PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE only); a regression in the map-roles-client-scope evaluation path (e.g. a typo'd scope constant or a broken hasPermission lookup) would ship silently and deny or allow client-scope role mapping at runtime with no failing test.

[BUG] The removal-event handler is now gated solely on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so for realms running the V2 fine-grained authz implementation (the V2 capability this PR targets, per the 'For V2 only' javadocs) the handler is skipped, and even if it ran, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException — meaning neither implementation cleans up permission resources when a client, role, or group is removed. Deleting a client/role/group in a V2-enabled realm leaves orphaned authorization resources, scopes, and scope-permission policies referencing the deleted entity in the realm's admin-permissions resource server; these accumulate indefinitely and are re-evaluated by hasPermission/hasGrantedPermission lookups (which resolve by entity id) whenever the admin-permissions evaluation path runs. Before this diff the cleanup ran unconditionally, so this is a dropped requirement with no replacement path anywhere in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE and the private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) helper are dead code — neither is referenced anywhere in the class — while canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException. The token-exchange requirement for the new Clients resource type was started and then dropped mid-implementation: the evaluator has no TOKEN_EXCHANGE scope in the CLIENTS scope set, no working canExchangeTo, and leftover scaffolding. Any code path that reaches the V2 exchangeTo surface gets an UnsupportedOperationException (500) rather than a proper deny, and future maintainers inherit unused imports and an uncalled 12-line method that imply a token-exchange feature that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] canView() (and the inherited canViewClientScopes(), which just returns canView()) grants access only via canViewClientDefault() or the VIEW scope, while canView(ClientScopeModel) additionally honors the MANAGE permission — so a caller granted all-clients MANAGE passes canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) but fails canView()/canViewClientScopes(). An admin delegated 'manage all clients' via a V2 permission can manage per-client default/optional scopes but is denied the realm-level client-scopes listing (requireViewClientScopes path), whereas under V1 the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role satisfied both; the inconsistent semantics make the delegated-admin experience differ depending on which endpoint the console calls.

[BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent handler calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which in V2 realms (MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting any client fails with a 500 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled and the realm routes to V2. Client removal in a V2 fine-grained-authz realm propagates UnsupportedOperationException out of the event listener inside the removal transaction, the DELETE returns 500 and the client is not removed; the same shape applies to the role/group branches via roles()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled.

[ADVISORY] All three entity-removal cleanup handlers were previously unconditional and are now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so permission artifacts created while the feature was enabled are never cleaned up after the feature is disabled. An operator who disables the feature (or had it on transiently) leaves orphaned authorization resources/policies referencing deleted clients, roles and groups; re-enabling the feature later surfaces stale permissions bound to non-existent entities, and the resource store accumulates garbage with no sweep path.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission runs a full root.evaluatePermission (policy-store query and evaluation) inside the resourceStore.findByType callback for every client resource in the realm, making the admin client-list path O(N) permission evaluations. In a realm with thousands of clients (or once per-client permission resources accumulate), every admin clients().findAll() that needs filtering triggers N sequential policy evaluations, each hitting the policy store — the listing endpoint degrades linearly with resource count and there is no pagination or batching on this hot path.

[ADVISORY] The permission-evaluation loop (evaluatePermission + nested scope scan) is duplicated three times in this one class — hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String,String), and hasGrantedPermission — and the copies have already drifted: hasGrantedPermission re-resolves root.realmResourceServer() per call while the other two early-return on isAdminSameRealm. The next scope/evaluation change (e.g., adding cross-realm guards or a scope-normalization step) must be applied in three places plus the UserPermissionsV2 copies; a fix applied to two of the three leaves a silently inconsistent authorization path that is very hard to detect in review.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is private and never called anywhere in the class — canExchangeTo throws before any evaluation context could be built. Dead code that implies a working token-exchange evaluation path exists in V2; a future implementer wiring token exchange may bind to this stub-shaped method (which builds a ClientModelIdentity but is never exercised) instead of designing the real path, inheriting its untested attribute setup ("kc.client.id").

[BUG] Twelve methods of the shared ClientPermissionEvaluator interface (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, and the other mapRoles*Permission variants) are implemented as bare UnsupportedOperationException throws, so any existing caller of the interface that runs in a V2 realm gets a 500 instead of a denial or a V2-equivalent answer. Legacy surfaces that call these methods — e.g., the client 'management/permissions' admin endpoints (getPermissions/resource/isPermissionsEnabled) and the token-exchange authorization check (canExchangeTo) — return an opaque server error in V2 realms rather than a 4xx or a graceful unsupported response; the fat interface keeps V1-only operations as compile-checked obligations that V2 cannot honor.

[ADVISORY] findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also matches the 'all-clients' type resource (created by getResourceTypeResource with the same type), so when the caller holds an all-clients grant the literal string "Clients" — not a client id — is added to the granted set that the consumer filters the client list by. Correctness of the client-list filtering now silently depends on the caller special-casing the magic resource name "Clients" inside a Set<String> of client ids; if the consumer instead intersects ids, an all-clients grant yields an unmatchable id and the admin sees an empty (or wrong) client list — an undocumented cross-module contract keyed on a display name.

[BUG] The entire removal-event cleanup listener was silently wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` during review iterations — a behavior change to existing legacy V1 cleanup that is unrelated to the PR's stated objective of adding a Client resource type, and that no human acceptance covers. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ disabled (the default for realms relying on legacy V1 admin permissions), role/client/group deletion no longer calls setPermissionsEnabled(..., false); the V1 permission resources and policies for the deleted entity are silently orphaned in the database, so legacy deployments accumulate stale permission state after every deletion. This is a silent change of the objective: the PR title promises a schema addition, but review iterations smuggled in a behavioral restriction of existing functionality.

[BUG] With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent handler now routes to the V2 evaluator: `management(...).clients()` returns the newly added ClientPermissionsV2, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` (ClientPermissionsV2.java, lines ~192-196) unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` — so the cleanup the listener was re-armed to perform crashes instead of cleaning up. Deleting any client in a realm with the feature enabled throws UnsupportedOperationException from inside the removal event, failing/rolling back the client deletion with a 500. The gating added in review actually makes this worse: it ensures the handler runs precisely in the configuration where the called method throws.

[BUG] `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` contradicts the contract the same diff documents in ClientPermissionEvaluator: when a per-client resource already exists (created by any earlier per-client permission), the method evaluates only that resource's policies and never consults the all-clients type resource, so an explicit "permission to MANAGE/VIEW all clients" is ignored for exactly the clients that have per-client resources. An admin granted all-clients MANAGE per the documented "For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to ... all clients" contract is denied manage/view on any client for which someone previously created a single-client permission (e.g., a VIEW grant for another admin) — access silently regresses depending on whether an unrelated per-client permission happens to exist, and the granted all-clients policy has no effect.

[ADVISORY] The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` has no call site anywhere in the new class — its only would-be consumer, `canExchangeTo`, immediately throws UnsupportedOperationException. Dead code shipped in the artifact; the next author touching token-exchange behavior in V2 must first determine whether this half-implemented evaluation context (with its custom `kc.client.id` attribute) is live or vestigial. Deletion test passes: removing it removes ~12 lines and one import with no functional change.

[ADVISORY] The new scope `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` is wired into the CLIENTS resource type and given a V2 evaluator implementation (`canMapClientScopeRoles` in ClientPermissionsV2), but no test in this diff exercises it — the map-roles test covers MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE only. A regression in the map-roles-client-scope evaluation path (the wrong scope constant, a copy-paste to MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, or the all-clients fallback miss) ships silently; anyone adding client-scope role-mapping restrictions later inherits unverified behavior in a security-sensitive check.

[ADVISORY] canMapClientScopeRoles and its new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope have no test anywhere in this diff, so a regression there (e.g., the evaluator checking the wrong scope constant) ships undetected. Checked the test files in the diff: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java (the only new client-permission test file) imports and exercises only CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and VIEW; no test grants or exercises map-roles-client-scope, so the branch `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)` (ClientPermissionsV2.java lines ~96-99) can silently regress and users granted that scope via the new schema would be denied (or denied users granted) role mapping via client scopes.

[ADVISORY] The hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) branch of canView(ClientScopeModel) is never exercised: testManageOnlyOneClient only touches client scopes after a MANAGE grant, and testViewAllClients never invokes any client-scope endpoint under its VIEW-only grant. Checked PermissionClientTest.java: under the VIEW-all permission the test calls findAll(true), protocol mappers, and create — but never getDefaultClientScopes/list client scopes — so if the VIEW branch of canView(ClientScopeModel) regresses (e.g., only MANAGE accepted), users with view-all-clients grants lose access to default/optional client scope listing with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] The newly added Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard around all three removal-event branches in AdminPermissions.onEvent has no test in this diff exercising either branch. Checked all test files in the diff (AbstractPermissionTest.java, PermissionClientTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java) — none touches role/client/group removal with the feature on or off, so the behavioral change (with the feature disabled, deleting a client/role/group no longer calls setPermissionsEnabled(false)) is unverified; a regression re-inverting the guard or misplacing it would not fail any test.

[ADVISORY] The getClientByClientId fallback branch in the new resolveClient method is never triggered by any test in this diff — every createPermission call passes a client UUID. Checked PermissionClientTest.java and UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java: all calls go through createPermission(client, <id>, ...) with myclient.getId()/user ids, so `session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id)` is dead in tests; a regression swapping the lookup order or breaking the by-clientId resolution (which operators using clientId strings in policies would hit) passes the suite green.

[ADVISORY] The pre-grant negative check in testManageOnlyOneClient couples getDefaultClientScopes() and removeDefaultClientScope() in one try block, so the asserted ForbiddenException can come from the get call and the 'remove default scope is denied without permission' claim is never actually verified. When the assertion passes, the reader cannot tell which operation was denied; if a regression makes removeDefaultClientScope permitted pre-grant while getDefaultClientScopes stays denied, this block still passes — the denial of scope removal before grant is only covered indirectly by testConfigureOnlyOneClient (CONFIGURE grant), never under a no-permission state.

[ADVISORY] The private getEvaluationContext method is dead code — its only logical caller, canExchangeTo, throws UnsupportedOperationException before it could ever be reached — and no test in the diff pins the UnsupportedOperationException contract of any V2-unsupported method. Checked the diff's test files: no test invokes canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission/mapRolesPermission/managePermission/setPermissionsEnabled in V2 mode, so (a) the dead method survives review and rots, and (b) if a V2 code path (e.g., token-exchange endpoint or the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calling setPermissionsEnabled) reaches these methods, it surfaces as an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (500) with no failing test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The newly added createClientPolicy helper has no caller in this diff, so the client-policy condition of the new permission evaluation (e.g., restricting a Clients-type permission to specific service accounts via a client policy) is untested. Checked PermissionClientTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — only createUserPolicy is used; if the helper is genuinely unused it should be deleted (deletion test passes: removing it removes an unexercised code path), and if it was intended for a truncated test the client-policy-based authorization path for the new Clients resource type currently has zero coverage — a policy-matching regression would grant or deny all-clients permissions without any test failing.

[ADVISORY] testViewAllClients asserts the post-grant 'can't create a client' denial with clients().create(null), relying on the authorization filter running before null-body deserialization; any change in filter ordering or body validation turns this into a 400/500 and the test fails for the wrong reason (or, if a 400 were returned, the equality assertion catches it but the test no longer tests authorization). Future maintainers get a flaky/misleading failure unrelated to permission logic; passing a real ClientRepresentation (as testManageAllClients does for the same negative check) would pin the authorization behavior unambiguously.

[ADVISORY] Wrapping all three entity-removal cleanup branches in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` means permission artifacts are no longer cleaned up when the feature is disabled, changing previously unconditional cleanup into feature-conditional cleanup. An operator who enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (creating per-client/per-role/per-group permission resources, policies, and scope permissions in the authz store), then disabled the feature, and then deletes a client/role/group leaves all associated permission rows orphaned in the database with no cleanup path; when the feature is re-enabled later, those stale rows persist forever and are never garbage-collected, since re-running deletion is impossible (the entity is gone). This is a data-hygiene regression relative to the review-base behavior, where the listener ran unconditionally on every removal event.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.java (line 92) calls exactly this method via management(...).clients(), so whenever the V2 permission implementation is resolved while the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate passes, client removal fails with an unhandled RuntimeException surfaced as a 500. Deleting a client in a deployment where both the FGAP feature gate passes and the V2 evaluators are selected turns a routine delete into a 500 for the admin; the same applies to role and group removal via the sibling listener branches. The gate added in this diff (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) keys on the V1 feature while the V2 implementation selection is independent, so the both-enabled combination reaches the throwing method.

[BUG] The removal-event cleanup (disable/delete stored permissions on RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, GroupRemovedEvent) is now silently skipped entirely when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is not enabled, including deployments running only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, which still creates per-entity permission resources via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource. Under a V2-enabled/V1-disabled deployment, every client/role/group deletion leaves its permission Resource, policies and grants orphaned in the realm's authorization store — the work is dropped with no log and no error — so the realm accumulates stale permission artifacts that still appear in permission listings and must be cleaned manually.

[BUG] getClientsWithPermission iterates findByType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), which includes the type-level 'all-clients' resource itself, and adds resource.getName() to the granted set — so when an all-clients permission grants the scope, the literal string "Clients" is returned as if it were a client ID, and if only the type-level permission exists the set contains no real client IDs at all. Callers that filter or enumerate permitted client IDs by membership in this set silently miss every client granted via the all-clients permission (the set holds "Clients", not IDs), or treat "Clients" as a valid client ID; the drop is invisible because the method returns a non-empty, success-shaped set.

[ADVISORY] The evaluate-permission-then-match-scope loop is duplicated three times in this class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission), each with its own Arrays.asList(scope) wrapper and contains() matching instead of a single equals/Set check. The next change to grant matching (e.g., supporting scope sets, fixing evaluation semantics, or adding logging) must be applied in three places in this file alone; missing one yields silently divergent grant behavior between the per-client, all-clients, and listing paths.

[ADVISORY] The new resolveClient fallback to session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id) is not exercised by any test in this diff — every client permission test passes the internal UUID (myclient.getId()), so only the getClientById branch is covered. A regression in the clientId fallback branch (e.g., returning the clientId instead of the internal id, or resolving across realms) would silently key permission resources by the wrong identifier, making admin-granted client permissions never match at evaluation time — a deny-by-default silent failure no test would catch.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canView()` is implemented as `return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW);` and does not honor the `MANAGE` permission (added for V2) at all. However, `canView(ClientScopeModel)` explicitly treats `MANAGE` as sufficient (`return hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)` when not covered by admin roles). The interface Javadoc in the diff states `canViewClientScopes()` “Returns true if canView() returns true”, so a caller granted all-clients `MANAGE` via V2 permissions can pass `canManageClientScopes()` / `canView(ClientScopeModel)` but still fail `canView()` / `canViewClientScopes()`, creating an inconsistent and likely broken authorization experience for realm-level client-scope listing vs per-client operations.

An operator who disables the feature (or had it on transiently) leaves orphaned authorization resources/policies referencing deleted clients, roles and groups; re-enabling the feature later surfaces stale permissions bound to non-existent entities, and the resource store accumulates garbage with no sweep path.

adjudication.rationale: In services/.../AdminPermissions.java, the listener’s entity-removal handlers (RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, GroupRemovedEvent) are now executed only inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. This means that if fine-grained authz was previously enabled (so artifacts could exist) and is later disabled, subsequent removals will no longer call `...setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` to clean up permission artifacts for deleted roles/clients/groups. The diff shows no alternative cleanup path, so orphaned authorization data can accumulate and later re-enabling could expose stale permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission runs a full root.evaluatePermission (policy-store query and evaluation) inside the resourceStore.findByType callback for every client resource in the realm, making the admin client-list path O(N) permission evaluations. In a realm with thousands of clients (or once per-client permission resources accumulate), every admin clients().findAll() that needs filtering triggers N sequential policy evaluations, each hitting the policy store — the listing endpoint degrades linearly with resource count and there is no pagination or batching on this hot path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission which iterates all client resources via resourceStore.findByType(..., resource -> { ... }) and, for each resource, calls hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope). hasGrantedPermission performs root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server), i.e., a full permission evaluation per resource. This is a linear per-resource evaluation pattern on client listing/filtering paths and can degrade with many client resources; it’s a performance/scalability concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The permission-evaluation loop (evaluatePermission + nested scope scan) is duplicated three times in this one class — hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String,String), and hasGrantedPermission — and the copies have already drifted: hasGrantedPermission re-resolves root.realmResourceServer() per call while the other two early-return on isAdminSameRealm. The next scope/evaluation change (e.g., adding cross-realm guards or a scope-normalization step) must be applied in three places plus the UserPermissionsV2 copies; a fix applied to two of the three leaves a silently inconsistent authorization path that is very hard to detect in review.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, the permission evaluation pattern is indeed duplicated in three methods: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)`, each doing `root.evaluatePermission(...)` followed by nested loops scanning `permission.getScopes()`. These copies are not identical: `hasPermission(...)` methods guard with `if (!root.isAdminSameRealm()) return false;` and null-check the `ResourceServer`, while `hasGrantedPermission(...)` does neither and re-fetches `ResourceServer server = root.realmResourceServer()` internally. In this diff it’s not a directly verifiable functional bug because `hasGrantedPermission` is currently only called from `getClientsWithPermission`, which already checks `isAdminSameRealm()` and `server != null`, but the drift/duplication is a concrete maintainability risk grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is private and never called anywhere in the class — canExchangeTo throws before any evaluation context could be built. Dead code that implies a working token-exchange evaluation path exists in V2; a future implementer wiring token exchange may bind to this stub-shaped method (which builds a ClientModelIdentity but is never exercised) instead of designing the real path, inheriting its untested attribute setup ("kc.client.id").

[BUG] Twelve methods of the shared ClientPermissionEvaluator interface (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, and the other mapRoles*Permission variants) are implemented as bare UnsupportedOperationException throws, so any existing caller of the interface that runs in a V2 realm gets a 500 instead of a denial or a V2-equivalent answer. Legacy surfaces that call these methods — e.g., the client 'management/permissions' admin endpoints (getPermissions/resource/isPermissionsEnabled) and the token-exchange authorization check (canExchangeTo) — return an opaque server error in V2 realms rather than a 4xx or a graceful unsupported response; the fat interface keeps V1-only operations as compile-checked obligations that V2 cannot honor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new V2 implementation (`ClientPermissionsV2`) where many inherited operations are implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `*Permission(...)`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). Also `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is changed to return this V2 implementation, so any existing code path that still calls those methods in V2 would now fail at runtime. However, the finding’s claim that these are “methods of the shared ClientPermissionEvaluator interface” is not shown in the diff (the interface file only adds Javadoc), and the diff does not show the callers/endpoints that would invoke these methods, so the asserted 500s vs 4xx cannot be verified solely from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also matches the 'all-clients' type resource (created by getResourceTypeResource with the same type), so when the caller holds an all-clients grant the literal string "Clients" — not a client id — is added to the granted set that the consumer filters the client list by. Correctness of the client-list filtering now silently depends on the caller special-casing the magic resource name "Clients" inside a Set<String> of client ids; if the consumer instead intersects ids, an all-clients grant yields an unmatchable id and the admin sees an empty (or wrong) client list — an undocumented cross-module contract keyed on a display name.
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: getClientsWithPermission is collecting the name of the type-level/all-clients "Clients" resource (via findByType) rather than actual per-client resource identifiers, but downstream logic expects real client IDs (e.g., for realm.getClientById / list filtering). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The entire removal-event cleanup listener was silently wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` during review iterations — a behavior change to existing legacy V1 cleanup that is unrelated to the PR's stated objective of adding a Client resource type, and that no human acceptance covers. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ disabled (the default for realms relying on legacy V1 admin permissions), role/client/group deletion no longer calls setPermissionsEnabled(..., false); the V1 permission resources and policies for the deleted entity are silently orphaned in the database, so legacy deployments accumulate stale permission state after every deletion. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent handler now routes to the V2 evaluator: `management(...).clients()` returns the newly added ClientPermissionsV2, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` (ClientPermissionsV2.java, lines ~192-196) unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` — so the cleanup the listener was re-armed to perform crashes instead of cleaning up. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` contradicts the contract the same diff documents in ClientPermissionEvaluator: when a per-client resource already exists (created by any earlier per-client permission), the method evaluates only that resource's policies and never consults the all-clients type resource, so an explicit "permission to MANAGE/VIEW all clients" is ignored for exactly the clients that have per-client resources. An admin granted all-clients MANAGE per the documented "For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to ... all clients" contract is denied manage/view on any client for which someone previously created a single-client permission (e.g., a VIEW grant for another admin) — access silently regresses depending on whether an unrelated per-client permission happens to exist, and the granted all-clients policy has no effect.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first resolves a per-client resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` and, if it exists, evaluates permissions **only** against that resource. The fallback to the all-clients resource type (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(... CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) happens only when the per-client resource is `null`. Therefore, if an all-clients permission (e.g. `MANAGE`/`VIEW` on the `Clients` resource type) is granted, it will be ignored for any client that already has a per-client resource created by some other permission. This contradicts the documented contract in `ClientPermissionEvaluator` (“For V2 only: ... permission to ... all clients”) and can cause access to regress depending on whether a per-client resource exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Wrapping all three entity-removal cleanup branches in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` means permission artifacts are no longer cleaned up when the feature is disabled, changing previously unconditional cleanup into feature-conditional cleanup. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.java (line 92) calls exactly this method via management(...).clients(), so whenever the V2 permission implementation is resolved while the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate passes, client removal fails with an unhandled RuntimeException surfaced as a 500. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The removal-event cleanup (disable/delete stored permissions on RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, GroupRemovedEvent) is now silently skipped entirely when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is not enabled, including deployments running only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, which still creates per-entity permission resources via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getClientsWithPermission iterates findByType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), which includes the type-level 'all-clients' resource itself, and adds resource.getName() to the granted set — so when an all-clients permission grants the scope, the literal string "Clients" is returned as if it were a client ID, and if only the type-level permission exists the set contains no real client IDs at all. Callers that filter or enumerate permitted client IDs by membership in this set silently miss every client granted via the all-clients permission (the set holds "Clients", not IDs), or treat "Clients" as a valid client ID; the drop is invisible because the method returns a non-empty, success-shaped set.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and unconditionally adds `resource.getName()` when `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)` is true. The diff shows the type-level “all clients” resource is identified by name `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (i.e., the literal string "Clients"), e.g. `hasPermission(String scope)` does `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())`. Therefore, when a scope is granted via the type-level resource, `getClientsWithPermission` will add the literal "Clients" to the returned set instead of any real client id(s). If only the type-level permission exists, the result is a non-empty set containing only "Clients", which is not a client id and would cause callers expecting client ids to mis-handle or miss the intended grant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The evaluate-permission-then-match-scope loop is duplicated three times in this class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission), each with its own Arrays.asList(scope) wrapper and contains() matching instead of a single equals/Set check. The next change to grant matching (e.g., supporting scope sets, fixing evaluation semantics, or adding logging) must be applied in three places in this file alone; missing one yields silently divergent grant behavior between the per-client, all-clients, and listing paths.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, similar permission-evaluation loops appear in multiple methods: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)` and `hasPermission(String)` both call `root.evaluatePermission(...)` and then iterate `Permission -> scopes` while building `expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope)` and using `expectedScopes.contains(s)`. `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)` repeats the same evaluate+iterate pattern (using `scope.equals(s)` instead). This is a concrete duplication/maintainability issue introduced by the diff: any future change to scope-matching semantics or logging would need to be applied in several places, risking divergence between per-client, all-clients, and listing checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new resolveClient fallback to session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id) is not exercised by any test in this diff — every client permission test passes the internal UUID (myclient.getId()), so only the getClientById branch is covered. A regression in the clientId fallback branch (e.g., returning the clientId instead of the internal id, or resolving across realms) would silently key permission resources by the wrong identifier, making admin-granted client permissions never match at evaluation time — a deny-by-default silent failure no test would catch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient(KeycloakSession, String) that first resolves by internal id (getClientById) and then falls back to clientId (getClientByClientId). In the new/updated client permission tests (e.g., PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient/testConfigureOnlyOneClient), permissions are created using myclient.getId() as the resource id (createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, ...)), which exercises only the getClientById branch. No test in this diff appears to pass a clientId string into resource creation so the fallback branch is untested. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly introduced identifier-resolution behavior, not an immediately verifiable defect.
